Remove pip-tools and legacy linter leftovers
description:
The project has fully migrated to uv (uv.lock + pyproject.toml with [project.optional-dependencies] and PEP 735 [dependency-groups]), and to ruff for linting/formatting. Several files from the previous pip-tools and flake8/pylint setup are still checked in. They are unreferenced by src/, tests/, justfile and pyproject.toml, and one of them documents a setup path that is broken.

Files to remove:

- requirements.in - pins toml==0.10.2, python-dotenv==1.1.0. Superseded by pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] extras.
- dev-requirements.in - pins ruff, pyright, python-dotenv, coverage, vulture, rust-just, pytest, pytest-cov. Superseded by pyproject.toml [dependency-groups] dev, which carries newer pins.
- dev-requirements.txt - 139-line pip-compile output. Superseded by uv.lock.
- update_requirements_in.py - 125-line helper that rewrites a .in file from a .txt file. Both inputs are obsolete, so the script has no purpose.
- .flake8 - flake8 config. Ruff lint config lives in pyproject.toml [tool.ruff.lint]. Nothing invokes flake8 (no justfile target, not in the dev dependency group).
- .pylintrc - pylint config. Same reasoning; pylint is not installed or invoked anywhere.

Documentation fix (this is a real bug, not just tidying):

README.md 'Development' section (around lines 73-79) instructs:

    virtualenv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip3 install -r dev-requirements.txt -r requirements.txt
    add2virtualenv src

requirements.txt does not exist in the repo, so this command fails for anyone following the README today. dev-requirements.txt would also be deleted by this issue. Replace the section with the uv workflow that the justfile already assumes, e.g. 'uv sync' (which installs the dev dependency group), and drop the virtualenv/add2virtualenv steps. The rest of the Development section (just fmt / just lint / just test) is accurate and should stay.

Note: README also references 'just test-docker' and 'tox and setup.py', but the justfile has no test-docker target and there is no setup.py or tox config. Worth checking while editing that section.
acceptance:
- The six files listed above are deleted from the repo.
- No remaining reference to them anywhere: grep -rn 'requirements\.\(in\|txt\)\|update_requirements_in\|flake8\|pylintrc' over the repo (excluding .git, uv.lock, and ruff's flake8-* rule-name comments in pyproject.toml) returns nothing.
- README Development section documents a setup that actually works, based on uv sync.
- just lint, just lint-pyright and just test all still pass after the removal.

json_file()/toml_file() field assignments fail type checking
description:
Assigning json_file() or toml_file() to a config field does not type check under pyright strict, even though it is the library's intended usage pattern.

The pattern:

    class AppConfig(BaseConfig):
        _prefix = "app"
        devices: dict[str, Any] = json_file(Path(...) / "devices.json")

json_file() is annotated to return JSONFile (src/voecfg/file.py:55), toml_file() returns TOMLFile (src/voecfg/file.py:60). The declared field type is whatever the loaded data will be — dict[str, Any] above. A type checker sees JSONFile assigned to dict[str, Any] and reports:

    error: Type "JSONFile" is not assignable to declared type "dict[str, Any]"
      "JSONFile" is not assignable to "dict[str, Any]" (reportAssignmentType)

The assignment is only correct at runtime because _Base._setup() detects the File instance and replaces it with its loaded contents (src/voecfg/base.py, the 'elif isinstance(value, File): setattr(self, member, value.load())' branch). Static checkers cannot see that substitution.

Why this matters: any user running pyright or mypy in strict mode against their own config classes hits this on every file-backed field, and their only recourse today is a per-line ignore. It is a papercut in the library's headline feature, not in their code.

Evidence in this repo: four sites in tests/test_voecfg1.py (lines 144, 153, 232, 241) now carry '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' purely because of this. Those were added as part of basecfg-57bf to get pyright to zero; they are suppressions, not fixes, and should be removed once this is solved.

Note _config_path is unaffected — it is declared 'File | str | Path | None' (src/voecfg/base.py), which accepts a File directly. Only the data-carrying fields have the mismatch.

Possible directions, none decided:
- Annotate json_file()/toml_file() as returning Any, so the assignment checks against any declared field type. Simple, but callers lose File typing entirely.
- Give the loaders a generic/overloaded signature so the return type follows the annotation at the assignment site.
- Keep the runtime behaviour but document a supported idiom (e.g. a typed descriptor) that checks cleanly.
- Provide a mypy/pyright plugin. Almost certainly disproportionate for this library.

Pick a direction with the maintainer before implementing.
acceptance:
- A config class assigning json_file() or toml_file() to a field of the loaded data's type passes pyright in strict mode with no per-line ignore.
- The four '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' comments at tests/test_voecfg1.py lines 144, 153, 232, 241 are removed and just lint-pyright still reports 0 errors.
- Existing runtime behaviour is unchanged: just test still passes, including test_load_json, test_load_toml, test_load_json_invalid and test_load_toml_invalid.
- README documents the type-checked idiom if it differs from what is shown today.

title: json_file()/toml_file() field assignments fail type checking
description:
Assigning json_file() or toml_file() to a config field does not type check under pyright strict, even though it is the library's intended usage pattern.

The pattern:

    class AppConfig(BaseConfig):
        _prefix = "app"
        devices: dict[str, Any] = json_file(Path(...) / "devices.json")

json_file() is annotated to return JSONFile (src/voecfg/file.py:55), toml_file() returns TOMLFile (src/voecfg/file.py:60). The declared field type is whatever the loaded data will be — dict[str, Any] above. A type checker sees JSONFile assigned to dict[str, Any] and reports:

    error: Type "JSONFile" is not assignable to declared type "dict[str, Any]"
      "JSONFile" is not assignable to "dict[str, Any]" (reportAssignmentType)

The assignment is only correct at runtime because _Base._setup() detects the File instance and replaces it with its loaded contents (src/voecfg/base.py, the 'elif isinstance(value, File): setattr(self, member, value.load())' branch). Static checkers cannot see that substitution.

Why this matters: any user running pyright or mypy in strict mode against their own config classes hits this on every file-backed field, and their only recourse today is a per-line ignore. It is a papercut in the library's headline feature, not in their code.

Evidence in this repo: four sites in tests/test_voecfg1.py (lines 144, 153, 232, 241) now carry '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' purely because of this. Those were added as part of basecfg-57bf to get pyright to zero; they are suppressions, not fixes, and should be removed once this is solved.

Note _config_path is unaffected — it is declared 'File | str | Path | None' (src/voecfg/base.py), which accepts a File directly. Only the data-carrying fields have the mismatch.

Possible directions, none decided:
- Annotate json_file()/toml_file() as returning Any, so the assignment checks against any declared field type. Simple, but callers lose File typing entirely.
- Give the loaders a generic/overloaded signature so the return type follows the annotation at the assignment site.
- Keep the runtime behaviour but document a supported idiom (e.g. a typed descriptor) that checks cleanly.
- Provide a mypy/pyright plugin. Almost certainly disproportionate for this library.

Pick a direction with the maintainer before implementing.
acceptance:
- A config class assigning json_file() or toml_file() to a field of the loaded data's type passes pyright in strict mode with no per-line ignore.
- The four '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' comments at tests/test_voecfg1.py lines 144, 153, 232, 241 are removed and just lint-pyright still reports 0 errors.
- Existing runtime behaviour is unchanged: just test still passes, including test_load_json, test_load_toml, test_load_json_invalid and test_load_toml_invalid.
- README documents the type-checked idiom if it differs from what is shown today.

comments.text:
Implemented the Any-return direction after prototyping the alternatives against pyright strict.

Why not the unbound TypeVar approach: it fixes the annotated case but the definition itself raises reportInvalidTypeVarUse ('TypeVar _T appears only once in generic function signature') and reportReturnType, and unannotated assignment collapses to Unknown, so '_config_path = json_file(...)' would start raising reportUnknownVariableType in user code. Change: src/voecfg/file.py json_file() and toml_file() now return Any instead of JSONFile/TOMLFile, with a comment recording that the value a caller ends up holding is the file's contents, not the File — _setup() swaps the attribute for load()'s result. This matches precedent: json.load() returns Any, and File.load() already did.

Removed the four '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' comments at tests/test_voecfg1.py lines 144, 153, 232, 241. The remaining ignore at line 429 ('value: str | int = 3.14') stays — different cause, it is a deliberate wrong-type fixture for the validation test, not a File issue.

- with git show HEAD:src/voecfg/file.py in place: error '"TOMLFile" is not assignable to "dict[str, Any]" (reportAssignmentType)'

- Annotate json_file()/toml_file() as returning Any, so the assignment checks against any declared field type. Simple, but callers lose File typing entirely.
- Give the loaders a generic/overloaded signature so the return type follows the annotation at the assignment site.
- Keep the runtime behaviour but document a supported idiom (e.g. a typed descriptor) that checks cleanly.
- Provide a mypy/pyright plugin. Almost certainly disproportionate for this library.

Pick a direction with the maintainer before implementing.

comments.text:
Implemented the Any-return direction after prototyping the alternatives against pyright strict.

Why not the unbound TypeVar approach: it fixes the annotated case but the definition itself raises reportInvalidTypeVarUse ('TypeVar _T appears only once in generic function signature') and reportReturnType, and unannotated assignment collapses to Unknown, so '_config_path = json_file(...)' would start raising reportUnknownVariableType in user code. That pattern is used throughout tests/test_voecfg1.py and example/example_usage.py:90, so that direction trades one broken pattern for another.

Change: src/voecfg/file.py json_file() and toml_file() now return Any instead of JSONFile/TOMLFile, with a comment recording that the value a caller ends up holding is the file's contents, not the File — _setup() swaps the attribute for load()'s result. This matches precedent: json.load() returns Any, and File.load() already did.

Removed the four '# pyright: ignore[reportAssignmentType]' comments at tests/test_voecfg1.py lines 144, 153, 232, 241. The remaining ignore at line 429 ('value: str | int = 3.14') stays — different cause, it is a deliberate wrong-type fixture for the validation test, not a File issue.

Verified with a before/after on example/example_usage.py:107, which is real user-style code outside the lint gate:
- with git show HEAD:src/voecfg/file.py in place: error '"TOMLFile" is not assignable to "dict[str, Any]" (reportAssignmentType)'
- with the fix: 'uv run pyright example' reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations

All four gates green after the change:
- just lint: All checks passed!
- just lint-pyright: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
- just test: 37 passed, 8 warnings in 0.76s
- just vulture: clean

No README change needed. The README never shows a json_file()/toml_file() field assignment, and the idiom users write is unchanged — it simply type checks now.

Known cost, accepted when picking this direction: the factory result is no longer checked at all, so 'count: int = json_file("devices.json")' is silently accepted. That annotation was never statically verifiable, since the file's shape is only known at runtime.
